text.p: Shares in French engineering conglomerate Alcatel Alsthom climbed strongly on Friday, bucking a weaker market, with brokers offering various possible factors.

One French analyst said there were rumours Alcatel would receive between two and three billion francs for an announced sale of its 20 percent stake in the Cofira holding company to British Telecommunications Plc. While the sale was not news, the rumoured amount was welcome, he added.
Alcatel was up 1.99 percent at 467.2 francs, on volume of 314,004 shares at 1105 GMT.
Ferri held the firm as a strong buy, fund managers said.

Fund managers said the Ferri analyst pointed to Alcatel's strong growth in orders in the telecoms sector, with 20 percent in the first six months and 16.7 percent in nine months. The company expects a double digit growth rate for the year, or even more if there is a big contract before the end of December.
The transmission sector has seen competitors leaving the market due to a sharp fall in prices and a return to profitability in 1997 was very probable, reckoned the analyst.
Alcatel is undervalued with capitalisation of $14 billion, compared with Ericsson's $18 billion, a feature liked by U.S. investors who have bought 15 percent of Alcatel, they said.
A U.S. broker said the shares were strong in New York and had benefited from U.S. institutional buying.
An Alcatel spokesman said he knew of no particular reason for the share price rise. The company had announced "a series of large contracts recently", he said.
Alcatel on Wednesday said won a one billion franc contract to supply mobile telephone equipment to the SFR unit of Cie Generale des Eaux.
On October 29, it said it had gained a two billion franc transatlantic cable contract.

The Alcatel spokesman reiterated chairman Serge Tchuruk's comment from September 26 that the group expected to make more than 10 billion francs in asset sales for the whole year, including the Cofira stake sale. Cofira is the company which holds SFR's capital.
In New York earlier this month, ADRs of major European telecommunications companies strengthened following the BT merger news with MCI Communications Corp.
Meanwhile, a French broker said a new fraud inquiry targeting Jean-Luc Lagardere, chairman of the Lagardere group, may have sparked hopes of a re-opening of the Thomson SA privatisation.
